subject: FrostBank intermittent model stalls — queued-request cordoning impacting checkout windows
messages:
From: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@frostbank.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@frostbank.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout timeouts — intermittent stalls since 03/14

Hi Marissa / Redwood support,

We started seeing intermittent stalls in our checkout flows yesterday afternoon (around 17:30 UTC). A subset of user requests hit long tails in model response time and return a 504 or a hard timeout in our gateway. This has caused multiple failed transactions and an uptick in error-rate for our fraud-scoring pipeline (we rely on your embeddings+rerank path).

Quick facts:
- Window: 2028-03-14 17:20–19:45 UTC (recurring incidents since then)
- Symptom: p99 for generation jumps to ~18s for ~0.4% of requests; overall error rate to our service ~3.2% during windows
- Impact: some batch scoring jobs fail and our checkout timeouts are closing the session for customers

I attached a short trace sample and our SLO report for the affected window (sample_traces.ndjson, slo_report.pdf). Can you confirm whether this is a broader platform problem or something specific to our instance?

We are on a Dedicated pool with regional routing in us-west-2. We have pinned the model to rw-large-2027-quant.

This is causing immediate business impact — please escalate internally and let us know mitigation steps and ETA. If you need to call, I'm available all day at +1-415-555-0123.

Thanks,
Peter Lowe
VP, Platform Engineering | FrostBank

---
Attachments: sample_traces.ndjson (ndjson), slo_report.pdf (pdf)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@frostbank.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout timeouts — intermittent stalls since 03/14

Peter — thanks for the trace bundle and the SLO snapshot. We're treating this as high priority. Short answer: we see the same p99 tail behavior in our telemetry for your pool and a correlated backlog in the request queue for the regional serving fleet.

Immediate actions I'm initiating now (will follow up as they complete):
- Gate 1 (short-term mitigation): reduce concurrency cap for the rw-large-2027-quant workers assigned to your pool to limit head-of-line blocking (15 min estimated).
- Gate 2: activate prefix/KV cache for stable historical prompts we saw in traces (eta 30 min).
- Routing: temporarily route heavy scoring traffic to an alternate, lightly loaded pool in the same region — this will increase capacity while we stabilize (requires your OK for a 1-hour maintenance window).
- Observability: Rishi and Vivek are looped in to monitor the queue depth, tail latency, and error-rate spikes.

Question for you: are you OK with a brief routing maintenance window where some requests may use an alternate quantized model variant (functionally equivalent for scoring) for up to 1 hour? That will help take pressure off the active pool.

I'll send a single-thread mitigation log and a proposed credit/compensation note once we have more signal.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1-650-555-0199

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: FrostBank — queued-request cordoning / executive attention request

Team — flagging FrostBank incident (see below). Customer is on Dedicated in us-west-2 and is experiencing long-tail stalls that are producing 504s at their gateway. They reported p99 ~18s and a customer-visible error-rate jump to ~3.2%. Traces attached.

Initial observations from our side:
- Telemetry shows a sustained backlog in the regional request queue pinned to a small set of scoring endpoints.
- Correlated spikes in KV cache misses and a pattern of large-batch scoring traffic that creates head-of-line blocking.
- Concurrency cap on one of the worker sets was left at the conservative default during a recent config push — that appears to be the limiting factor for this pool.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi / Infra: can you prioritize a config change to increase concurrency cap and ensure autoscaler weights are applied to this pool? I need an ETA and a rollback plan.
- Vivek / Support: please prepare a short mitigation runbook I can share with the customer (I attached mitigation_runbook.md).
- Laura / Sales Ops: I may need support approving a credit for March usage depending on impact. Please advise on template and escalation path.

Customer asks for an ETA and a clear compensation note. This is flaggable to the exec team if we can't stabilize within 4 hours.

I'll post updates to the thread as actions complete.

Thanks,
Marissa

---
Attachments: mitigation_runbook.md (text)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@frostbank.com>
Cc: support@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 17 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FrostBank intermittent model stalls — queued-request cordoning impacting checkout windows

Marissa / Peter / Team — final update and RCA summary. Apologies for the delayed wrap.

What happened (short RCA):
- Root cause: a recent config push to the us-west-2 dedicated serving pool accidentally reverted concurrency weights for the rw-large-2027-quant shard. The effective cap fell from 48 -> 8 in a subset of workers; the autoscaler did not recover fast enough due to a threshold mismatch.
- Consequence: queued requests accumulated behind long-running generations; KV cache misses increased because the slow tail requests evicted useful entries; head-of-line blocking produced the observed p99 spikes and a higher error-rate in downstream gateways.

What we did (mitigations applied):
- Increased concurrency cap back to 48 for the affected shard and corrected autoscaler thresholds (completed at 2028-03-15T19:20:00Z).
- Activated prefix KV cache and tuned TTLs for the scoring prompt families referenced in the traces (completed at 2028-03-15T19:50:00Z).
- Enabled a temporary routing rule to spill heavy scoring traffic to a spare regional pool (completed at 2028-03-15T20:05:00Z).
- Deployed a quick fallback to the smaller quantized model variant for batch scoring above a 2k token threshold (completed at 2028-03-15T20:20:00Z).

Outcome & metrics:
- Error rate for FrostBank dropped from ~3.2% to 0.12% during subsequent windows.
- p99 for generation for affected flows returned to ~1.1s median within 40 minutes of the cap change.
- Queue depth tail (99.99th) reduced by ~87% vs peak.

Follow-ups / permanent fixes:
- We'll add an automated guard to prevent concurrency caps from regressing below a safe threshold for dedicated pools (DR plan in progress).
- Improve autoscaler threshold tuning and add a backlog-based emergency scaling trigger.
- Postmortem draft attached for your review (postmortem-draft.md).

Customer compensation: Marissa / Laura — recommend an account credit equal to 10% of March committed usage and a technical review session. If you want me to produce the figures for approval, I can pull usage delta and cost impact.

Peter — sorry for the disruption and thanks for the patience. We're available to run a focused technical session with your platform team this week to walk the trace analysis and the mitigations we applied.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
